source_contract.goal: Preserve firmware-loaded initramfs_2712 bytes before early memory setup can overwrite them.
source_contract.strategy: Exclude FDT /chosen linux,initrd-start..linux,initrd-end from the Pi 5 early usable-memory candidate before bootstrap reservation, translation-table layout, allocator initialization, and cache transition.
source_contract.transport_goal_preserved: Pi 5 consumes firmware-loaded talos-generated-root-v1 artifact from FDT /chosen bounds instead of compiled generated-root fallback.

accepted_input_evidence.observed_blocker: source=compiled-fallback reason=missing-artifact after early memory setup overlapped the firmware initramfs range

memory_invariants: Early usable-memory candidate excludes any page intersecting present non-empty FDT /chosen initrd bounds.
Kernel image, DTB blob, FDT reservation entries, and /reserved-memory exclusions remain in force.
Low-tail policy remains conservative and does not claim high memory or generalized physical-memory ownership.
No valid candidate after exclusions remains an unavailable memory plan rather than allocation over firmware initramfs bytes.
Missing or invalid initrd bounds preserve compiled generated-root fallback behavior.

findings.finding: Selected reserve-by-memory-plan-exclusion as the concrete implementation boundary.
Mapped source owners and memory invariants needed by the next implementation task.
Implementation, local tests/builds, candidate archive review, and Pi 5 proof remain separate tasks.
TFTP fetch alone is not Pi 5 generated-root consumption proof.
Copy-first remediation, static maximum-size buffers, persistence, SD/USB/block drivers, networking, SSH, high-memory ownership, DMA-safe allocation, and phase transition are outside this task.
No hardware lock or inconclusive-run triage was needed for this static contract.
